items.summary: Google released emergency security updates for a new Chrome zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-125350, marking the eighth actively exploited flaw since the start of the year. The company stated it is aware an exploit exists and stems from a Use-After-Free weakness in the browser's XML component. Google has not shared further details about the incidents, noting restrictions may continue until most users are updated or if the bug affects third-party libraries. Fixes have rolled out to Windows, macOS (157. 0. 8103. 50/. 51), and Linux (157. 0. 8103.
items.title: Google Patches Eight Exploited Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in 2026

items.summary: Chromagraph Camera, a $12.99 app with no free trial or subscription, reached the top of Apple's paid Photo & Video charts last week. Director Rian Johnson credited cinematographer Steve Yedlin for building it to shoot RAW and bypass the iPhone's look processing using film-style image techniques.
items.title: Rian Johnson's Chromagraph Camera App Tops iPhone Charts

items.summary:
In a series profiling everyday jobs, Keith Fong, a 29-year-old mechanical engineer at STTGDC’s Tai Seng data centre in Singapore, describes his role ensuring uninterrupted power and cooling for AI workloads. He is one of four team leads in a 20-strong department that monitors the facility around the clock, including providing “remote hands” service to customers whose equipment it hosts. Fong says there must be no downtime at all, relying on resilience measures such as backup generators and uninterruptible power supplies when outages occur. The Tai Seng site has an IT load of 13. 7MW, and across STTGDC’s global data centres about 83% of electricity is renewable, he says. He recounts dropping everything to return to work after an alarm during a family celebration last Christmas. His team also replaced 10 rooftop chillers that are 39% more energy-efficient, a project planned over three years and executed in phases over a year.

visual null
items.title: A data centre engineer on keeping power and cooling running

items.summary: A DBS Bank survey, conducted in September by Kantar and released on Nov 10, found that half of the central banks polled are more interested in tapping Asian gold hubs like Singapore, drawn by new state-backed infrastructure for storing and trading gold. However, only a quarter of respondents said they are actively evaluating Asia-based hubs, suggesting implementation may still be distant. DBS officials noted trusted infrastructure is transforming access to gold as regional demand grows.
items.title: DBS Survey Finds Banks Eyeing Asian Gold Hubs

items.summary: Meta AI launched Muse Ember, which it describes as its smallest and most efficient model for complex reasoning execution like tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing. Priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output—matching GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5—it sits on the Artificial Analysis efficiency frontier, with Meta stating no model scores higher for less per task.
items.title: Meta AI Launches Muse Ember as a Low-Cost Reasoning Model

items.summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (BERC) has opened proceedings on a joint petition from South and North Bihar Power Distribution Companies seeking amendments to rooftop solar regulations. The proposal introduces a Feed-in-Tariff of ₹2.71 per kWh for surplus electricity under gross metering, payable to prosumers or third-party owners. After publishing the notice in newspapers following October 7, 2026 directions and receiving stakeholder submissions, BERC directed its Secretariat to share comments with petitioners; replies are due by November 19, 2026, ahead of a hearing on November 24, 2026. The outcome may shape rooftop solar metering rules for FY 2026-27 in Bihar.
items.title: BERC Reviews Proposed Rooftop Solar Feed-In Tariff for FY 2026-27 in Bihar

items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization reported that heat is accumulating in Earth’s systems at an accelerating rate as the COP31 climate summit begins in Antalya, Turkey. The energy imbalance between incoming and outgoing solar radiation reached its highest level since monitoring began, with 2026 on track to be one of the four warmest years on record. Global surface temperature for January through September was about 1.47 degrees C above preindustrial levels. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said humanity has entered a new age of climate extremes, while professor Bill McGuire warned that the 1.5 degree limit may be crossed permanently by 2028.
items.title: WMO Warns Climate Warming Is Accelerating Ahead of COP31

items.summary: The Safer Foundation runs a transitional center on Chicago’s West Side that prepares formerly incarcerated men and women for clean energy work. Through Illinois’ 2017 Future Energy Jobs Act and 2021 Climate and Equitable Jobs Act, the program offers skills training plus wraparound services such as counseling, financial literacy, and an on-site food pantry to help clients overcome barriers like criminal records and gaps in employment history. Safer says that over the past three years more than 100 people earned clean energy certifications through its training, with 79 of them securing jobs after completing it. Safer President Mark Yates describes solar as a promising entry-level field whose carpentry and electrical experience transfers to other industries, while trainee Vincent Jones now works as an instructor for the state’s clean energy programs.
items.title: Chicago nonprofit trains formerly incarcerated people for solar careers

items.summary: A Canary Media report traces how a hoped-for boom in domestic offshore wind manufacturing failed to materialize after the 2025 election. Early optimism followed federal incentives and leasing, with experts estimating nearly $23 billion of investment by 2030 was expected. Companies such as Ingeteam’s Milwaukee plant and Gulf Wind Technology pursued generators, blades and foundations, but economic headwinds and Trump administration stop-work orders reportedly set the industry back a decade. Firms are now pivoting to nuclear submarines, subsea cables and aerospace; analysts warn of long-term reputational damage and an electricity supply crunch ahead.
items.title: Offshore Wind Manufacturing Boom Fizzles in U.S.

items.summary: Research by New Energy Nexus (NEX) Philippines finds price wars are now the biggest challenge facing rooftop solar installers, surpassing earlier supply constraints. Sheryl Estella told pv magazine that combined weekly installations rose from around 30 to nearly 70 after an energy crisis began in March. She said buyers increasingly choose on price and pointed to clearer standards and Social Security System loans as possible support.
items.title: Price Wars Top Challenges for Philippine Solar Installers

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Friday that Tesla would end Cybertruck production next year after weak sales, making room for the Cybercab robotaxi. The truck sold just over 20,000 units last year versus a projected 250,000 vehicles annually before its late-2023 rollout; its starting price rose to $92,500 in 2026. Analysts and advocates note high prices, charging concerns, Musk’s politics, and partisan resistance over electric vehicles limited appeal. Krassner of the American EV Jobs Alliance said round one favored gas trucks but round two has not begun; Strategic Vision’s Alexander Edwards cautioned against calling it a failure. Ford is set to launch its Fathom pickup next year starting at $28,400.
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production for Cheaper Electric Trucks

items.summary: Chinese solar manufacturer DMEGC has unveiled the Infinity RT 3.0 series, a line of six bifacial glass-glass photovoltaic modules with steel frames built from zinc-aluminum-magnesium coated steel said to have nearly twice the tensile strength of conventional aluminum alloys. The design reportedly cuts rear-side shading by 76% and raises unshaded area by 3.6%, yielding a theoretical bifaciality gain of about 2.8%. Modules output between 640 W and 665 W at efficiencies from 23.7% to 24.6%, with simulations indicating annual generation of 2,078 kWh/kWp. DMEGC cites salt mist, ammonia corrosion and stress testing plus a 15-year product warranty and 30-year power output guarantee.
items.title: DMEGC Unveils Steel-Framed Bifacial Solar Module Series

items.summary: The United States is investigating whether Singapore-based cloud firm Megaspeed helped Beijing access restricted Nvidia AI chips, amid scrutiny of Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang. Business filings show Megaspeed was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International and renamed in March 2023; its assets rose to US$3 billion in 2024 from US$33 million in 2023, while revenue reached US$294 million. Singapore police are separately investigating the firm over suspected domestic-law breaches.
items.title: US probes Nvidia's Megaspeed customer over chip-export suspicions

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang began washing dishes at a Denny's in East San Jose, where he and two Sun Microsystems colleagues planned the GPU company in 1993. The chain marked that booth 'The Booth That Launched a $1 Trillion Company' and added his Nvidia Breakfast Bytes dish.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Denny's dish honors Nvidia's restaurant-born idea

items.summary: Nvidia's stock fell 4.3% as shareholders filed a proposed class action in California federal court, alleging the company and CEO Jensen Huang withheld material information about alleged ties to a former Megaspeed executive suspected of passing sensitive data to China. Shareholder Mark Kistenmacher leads the suit; Nvidia has launched an independent investigation while Huang faces an FBI probe and a closed-door meeting with U.S. lawmakers on November 18.
items.title: Nvidia Shareholders File Class Action Over Jensen Huang Allegations; Stock Falls 4.3%

items.summary: Infineon forecast more than 20 per cent revenue growth for 2027, with profitability rising about five percentage points. The German chipmaker reported fourth-quarter revenue of €4.706 billion ($5.28 billion) and a segment margin of 23.8 per cent, while full-year revenue rose 12 per cent to €16.353 billion. CEO Jochen Hanebeck cited cyclical recovery and demand from data centres, power infrastructure and software-defined cars. For 2027, Infineon forecasts around €20 billion in revenue, including close to €4 billion from data-centre power supplies, with adjusted free cash flow of about €2.2 billion.
items.title: Infineon Forecasts Strong 2027 Growth on Data-Centre Demand

items.summary: Kim Kardashian's Skims is refunding customers for its $148 (£110) advent calendar after social media mocked the low-quality contents. A spokesperson said some items 'didn't meet expectations' and that every customer was contacted about a full refund or credit.
items.title: Skims Offers Refunds After Advent Calendar Backlash

items.summary: The Welsh government says up to 20,000 households using heating oil could receive a £250 payment from £5m of a new £130m package. Deputy First Minister Sioned Williams called cost-of-living support a key priority and said the money provides immediate winter relief. The funds help off-grid households dependent on heating oil or LPG who qualify for council tax reduction, alongside existing energy payments and bus travel support.
items.title: Welsh Government Offers Heating Oil Households £250 Winter Payment

items.summary: Shopping data shows British households increased purchases of bottled water, tinned goods and hand sanitiser in the 10 days after the government's Be Ready campaign. Hand sanitiser sales surged 83%, bottled water rose 67% and tinned jarred goods up 37%. Fraser McKevitt of Worldpanel by Numerator said shoppers added recommended items rather than filling trolleys, with fewer than a third buying bottled water in October. The report also noted rising grocery inflation at 2.6% to 1 November (Worldpanel by Numerator).
items.title: UK Shoppers Stockpile Essentials Without Panic Buying

items.summary: Reuters profiles Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Known also as Huang Le, she built a finance career before becoming controlling shareholder of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an Nvidia cloud partner in Asia-Pacific. The New York Times reported US authorities concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset passing information to Beijing while close with the CEO; Reuters could not independently verify this allegation, which China has denied. Huang and Jensen Huang are not related.
items.title: Alice Huang's Finance-to-Chips Path Draws US Scrutiny Over Nvidia Ties

items.summary: Nvidia and its chief executive Jensen Huang face a shareholder lawsuit alleging they defrauded investors by hiding national security concerns tied to his alleged affair with Alice Huang, an ex-Megaspeed executive deemed a Chinese intelligence asset. The complaint was filed five minutes after market close; shares fell 4. 3%, cutting Nvidia's value by about $190bn. Trump said the FBI is investigating but that Huang will be in good shape. Nvidia launched its own independent probe and Huang posted an open letter pledging cooperation, saying he loves his country and company. He admitted being unfaithful to his wife without disclosing details of the relationship.
items.title: Shareholders Sue Nvidia and Jensen Huang Over Alleged Chinese Spy Affair

items.summary: A Victorian newsagent worker is linked to Megaspeed Australia, a company at the centre of an alleged spy scandal involving Nvidia's CEO. The firm appears registered as a subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed. A 29-year-old man lives in regional Victoria and is listed as its director, though his father told ABC News he had never heard of it. ASIC filings suggest mail to its Martin Place address could not be delivered in January.
items.title: Newsagent Worker Linked to Nvidia Scandal Firm

items.summary: US President Donald Trump says the FBI is investigating alleged links between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese government agent, whom US intelligence suspects of gathering information for Beijing. Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump said he had spoken to Huang earlier that day after asking whether he knew about the allegations; Huang denied knowing the person was a spy. Trump added he believes Huang's denial.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia CEO Over Spy Allegations

items.summary: A book titled 'Digital and Intelligent Transformation in Xizang: Shared Prosperity and Development' was launched Tuesday at the 10th Xizang Think Tank International Forum held at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in Beijing. The eight chapters document Xizang's digital development achievements, with experts describing it as an academic reference for scholars worldwide to study the region.
items.title: Book on Xizang's Digital Transformation Launched at Forum

items.summary: As the Asia-Pacific region prepares for the November 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Guangdong Province, China is promoting artificial intelligence as a driver of regional cooperation. The meeting's theme emphasizes openness, innovation and cooperation, with inclusive AI development highlighted as a priority. Chinese-developed open-source models reportedly account for 41% of global downloads per Hugging Face's Spring 2026 report, while its MAZU weather platform has reached eight countries and been cloud-accessed in more than 40 since 2024, according to Pakistan Today.
items.title: China Pushes AI Cooperation Ahead of APEC 2026 in Shenzhen

items.summary: Official data from the General Administration of Customs showed China's foreign trade in goods grew 20% year-on-year over January to October, accelerating from 18.8%, reaching 44.81 trillion yuan ($6.72 trillion). Imports surged 23.6% while exports rose 17.6%. The data points to a shift toward AI hardware and integrated circuits, which saw imports jump 58% and exports rise 101.9%. Trade with ASEAN grew 24.2%, leading regional partners.
items.title: China's Foreign Trade Growth Accelerates in First Ten Months of 2026

items.summary: The second China-Canada Strategic Economic and Financial Dialogue was held on Monday in Vancouver, co-chaired by Chinese vice premier He Lifeng and Canadian ministers Francois-Philippe Champagne and Maninder Sidhu. The participants issued statements about strengthening cooperation in economy, trade, finance and investment, with no figures or dates reported beyond the meeting itself.
items.title: China and Canada Hold Second Strategic Economic Dialogue in Vancouver

items.summary: President Trump's top envoy, along with negotiators from Russia and Ukraine, is in Abu Dhabi to resume peace talks aimed at ending the war. Audio of the meeting will be available later today.
items.title: Kushner and Witkoff Resume Peace Talks Between Russia and Ukraine

items.summary: President Trump has leaned toward diplomacy in the war with Iran following midterm election losses, according to reporting. The White House said audio would be available later that day.
items.title: Trump Signals Diplomacy With Iran After Midterm Defeats

items.summary: Kemi Badenoch launched the Conservative policy document Welfare That Works, outlining plans to cut welfare by £36bn. More than a third of savings would come from sickness and disability benefits. Labour responded that Tories cannot be trusted with problems they created, citing a record £33bn rise in the welfare bill under their government.
items.title: Badenoch defends £36bn Tory welfare cuts amid Labour criticism

items.summary: A police officer has died and another was injured after a backpack exploded while officers from Spain's Special Canine Unit examined it on Tuesday morning in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo, according to police. The deceased officer has been named as Juan José. Police paid tribute to him via a statement on X.
items.title: Police Officer Killed in Backpack Explosion in Oviedo

items.summary: At least 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death in the Democratic Republic of Congo for cowardice, mutiny and refusing orders, local media report. The sentences followed a trial of 71 soldiers before a military court in Walikale, North Kivu province; four were acquitted and one received a 10-year prison term. Soldiers had reportedly abandoned positions during clashes with FRN fighters.
items.title: DR Congo Sentences Soldiers to Death for Cowardice and Mutiny

items.summary: After nearly a century without gray wolves, the animals are recolonizing California and reshaping its ecosystems. Mongabay's Spoorthy Raman examines how this recovery is unfolding: conservationists welcome the return while ranchers blame livestock losses on them, prompting calls for coexistence amid growing wolf numbers.
items.title: Gray Wolves Return to California After Centuries of Absence

items.summary: Olga, a 49-year-old choreographer living near the Russian city of Kirov, woke to an explosion that shook her apartment building. Looking out, she saw black smoke rising from a military equipment factory hit by a missile. The strike killed six people and injured another 26, according to the local governor. Olga noted that Kirov is normally known for its monastery rather than war.
items.title: Missile strike on Kirov factory kills six, injures 26

items.summary: A poor Republican midterm showing has weakened Donald Trump's administration politically, raising questions about American foreign policy and Washington's commitment to longstanding alliances. These uncertainties are especially consequential in Northeast Asia, where U.S.-South Korea tensions threaten trilateral security cooperation with Japan since South Korean President Lee Jae Myung took office after a June 2025 snap election.
items.title: U.S.-South Korea alliance strains under Trump's weakened political standing

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday that artificial intelligence should be banned wherever it poses a risk to the mental health of children. He made the comments in an interview with Les Echos, ahead of adopting an AI protection charter at the Paris Peace Forum. The charter is intended to inform national and European legislative debates and will bring together companies including OpenAI and Anthropic.
items.title: Macron Calls for Banning AI That Risks Children's Mental Health

items.summary: More than 100 workers at South32's Worsley Alumina refinery have been on industrial action for two days, demanding better pay and conditions ahead of an $8 billion sale to US miner Alcoa. Unions allege staff earn less and work longer hours than comparable Alcoa employees, with discretionary bonuses potentially lost after the takeover. A South32 spokesperson said it remains engaged constructively.
items.title: South32 refinery workers strike over pay as Alcoa takeover looms

items.summary: UN Women warned that over 1. 5 billion women and girls, more than one-third of the global total, live in areas where climate hazards intersect with economic insecurity and gender inequality. The agency said 73% of countries acknowledge gender-specific climate risks but only slightly more than one-third address them fully. Under worst-case conditions, an additional 141 million women and girls could enter extreme poverty, and a 1C temperature rise was tied to women losing 34% more income than men in 24 countries, while prolonged droughts raised odds of sexual violence against adolescent girls by 21% across 14 nations.
items.title: UN Women Warns Billions of Women Face Climate Hotspots

items.summary: On Monday evening, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi received a phone call from British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to discuss containing Middle East tensions. The presidency said the two leaders focused on preventing conflict expansion, ensuring humanitarian aid access to Gaza and its reconstruction, and complying with the ceasefire agreement. Sisi called for international efforts to revive a political process toward an independent Palestinian state along June 4, 1967 borders. The call comes amid continued regional tensions linked to military confrontations involving the US, Israel and Iran since February, after fighting resumed in July following earlier understandings reached in April and June that later collapsed.
items.title: Egyptian and British Leaders Discuss Containing Iran Escalation, Gaza Ceasefire

items.summary: A military court in the Democratic Republic of Congo sentenced 66 soldiers to death, according to local media. The defendants were among 71 troops tried in Walikale, North Kivu province; four were acquitted and one received a 10-year prison sentence. DR Congo resumed capital punishment in March 2024 after two decades without executions.
items.title: DR Congo Court Sentences 66 Soldiers to Death for Fleeing Rebel Fighting

items.summary: The article explains how China obtains advanced Nvidia GPUs despite US export controls, which ban the top-end Blackwell and Rubin chips on security grounds. It outlines possible channels: physical smuggling of dismantled chips, as reported by The Information about DeepSeek; renting computing power in Southeast Asian data centres that remain compliant while users access them from within China; and growing reliance on domestic alternatives like Huawei's chips, whose next-generation AI chip is expected ready in the first quarter of 2027. Analysts note Nvidia hardware still accelerates top-level training but faces rising Chinese competition as homegrown options improve fast.
items.title: China's Routes for Nvidia Chips Amid US Restrictions

items.summary: Lawmakers and advocates say legislation is likely to tighten China's access to AI chips, following reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence agent. Three measures—the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, and the Match Act—are slated for possible inclusion in the fiscal year 2027 defense authorization bill. Nvidia opposes two of them; the company declined comment. Senators Warren and Banks called for decisive action.
items.title: Lawmakers Push Chip Restrictions After Nvidia-China Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic is planning an IPO marketing event with JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon, part of efforts for its potentially record-breaking listing. The offering may begin early Tuesday ahead of a Nasdaq debut before Thanksgiving, per Bloomberg. JPMorgan leads domestic retail marketing among 22 banks on the deal. Anthropic weighs a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of shares, targeting valuations of $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion after midterms reshaped AI pricing.
items.title: Anthropic Schedules IPO Marketing Event With JPMorgan’s Dimon

items.summary: Nvidia fell about 4.3 per cent on November 9, wiping out approximately $190 billion from its market capitalisation, Reuters reported. A proposed class-action lawsuit filed that day accuses Nvidia and chief executive Jensen Huang of concealing an alleged relationship with Alice Huang, suspected to work for Chinese intelligence, raising national security concerns shareholders say they were not told about. The complaint was led by Mark Kistenmacher and sought unspecified damages. Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to employees on November 8; his board launched an investigation. Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China has denied.
items.title: Nvidia Loses $190 Billion as CEO Affair and Lawsuit Mount

items.summary: A day after three contract workers were killed, Apple reportedly sent a team to investigate the deaths of three contract workers at Tata Electronics’ iPhone components factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The incident occurred on Monday during maintenance work on an effluent treatment plant operated by Nalco Water, part of US-headquartered Ecolab; district official Dinesh Kumar said the workers died when they inhaled gas while inspecting a nano-filtration tank. Apple and Tata will investigate alongside state authorities. Nalco Water called it “extremely serious” and said its sub-contractor engaged the workers. There has been no production impact as the facility was closed for Deepavali. Tata Electronics accounts for roughly 40 percebnt of iPhone assembly, with Foxconn making up the rest; India now produces about 25% of world iPhones.
items.title: Apple and Tata Investigate Three Worker Deaths at Tamil Nadu iPhone Parts Factory

items.summary: A Tata Electronics factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, where Apple iPhones are assembled, killed three contract workers by asphyxiation, prompting investigations from the company and state government. The incident is part of a pattern of problems at Apple's Indian suppliers since 2017, including fires, pollution warnings, labour disputes, and data breaches involving stolen files and photos of an unreleased iPhone model. Reuters documents these events across multiple facilities and years, noting that some investigations later cleared the companies involved while others found standards were not met.
items.title: Apple Supplier Facilities Face Repeated Disruptions in India

items.summary: Nvidia's board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang on November 8 after he admitted a relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence agencies believe worked for China. The probe has surfaced a question Nvidia never answered publicly: who leads the company if Huang cannot stay. Analysts at Melius Research say there is no clear successor and that his departure would be hard to price in. Governance experts warn the board lacks an identified heir and questions how it reached this point, while shareholders filed a class action suit accusing Nvidia of hiding ties to Alice Huang. For now, Huang remains CEO as he works to earn back confidence.
items.title: Nvidia Board Investigates Jensen Huang Amid Succession Worry

items.summary: Anna Konidala deactivated her Instagram account after the couple announced their separation, ending a 13-year marriage. The decision followed a joint statement issued on Monday stating they part ways with mutual understanding and respect while remaining devoted parents to their children. They requested privacy during this personal transition.
items.title: Anna Konidala Deactivates Instagram After Separation From Pawan Kalyan

items.summary: Jensen Huang dropped out of the world's top 10 richest after Nvidia shares fell, reducing his net worth to $148 billion per the Bloomberg Billionaires Index update dated Nov 10. His fortune declined by $6.47 billion (4.2%) in the latest update and $15 billion (9.2%) over the preceding year.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Falls From World's Top 10 Richest After Net Worth Drop

items.summary: Three contract workers died on Monday evening while servicing a wastewater treatment tank at Tata Electronics' facility near Hosur, Tamil Nadu. Officials suspect the men inhaled toxic gas inside the tank operated by Nalco Water, an Ecolab unit hired through a subcontractor. The company and Apple have launched separate investigations as authorities probe safety arrangements.
items.title: Three workers die in gas inhalation at Tata iPhone factory

items.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested Farzad "Tony" Toutouni, an Iranian-born social media personality with over one million followers known for posts featuring luxury items and scantily clad women. ICE announced the detention on November 9 after he was held October 27. Officials allege he lived in the United States illegally despite a criminal record including forgery and robbery charges, and that he served more than 16 months in prison. He remains in custody pending removal proceedings.
items.title: ICE Arrests Influencer Known as 'Iranian King of Instagram'

items.summary: Meta made its Muse Ember, Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder models available through Google Cloud's Model Garden managed APIs. The multimodal models offer a one-million-token context window; Ember is described as the smallest option at roughly one-third the per-task cost of comparable models for sub-agent work. Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied to Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg, welcoming the collaboration and noting that Google Cloud would host and serve Meta's proprietary AI alongside its own Gemini offerings.
items.title: Google CEO welcomes Meta's AI models on Google Cloud

items.summary: Beijing's trade surplus passed $1 trillion in the first ten months of 2026, reaching $1.04 trillion and crossing the mark a month earlier than in 2025. October exports rose 35.2%, below September's 36.3% but above economists' 33.5% forecast, while imports grew 41.6%. The run is tied to AI-driven demand for high-tech goods and raises concerns about export dependence amid weak domestic spending and property-sector weakness.
items.title: China’s trade surplus tops $1 trn for second year in a row, exports jump 35.2% in October: What's leading the surge?

items.summary: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge defended former Mysore ruler Tipu Sultan on Tuesday, stating the RSS played no role in India's freedom struggle and citing a book praising him by ex-chief minister BS Yediyurappa. His remarks follow a memorandum from Tehrik-e-Khudadad urging reinstatement of Tipu Sultan Jayanti, which Congress introduced in 2015 but discontinued in 2019.
items.title: Karnataka minister defends Tipu Sultan, criticizes BJP history stance

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi, in her newly released memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, recounted that during a 2010 conversation Pranab Mukherjee hinted at a 'long-held desire' to become prime minister, leaving her 'shocked.' Her account drew sharp criticism from Sharmistha, his daughter, who questioned why such ambition should surprise anyone with decades of political experience. Sharmistha said there was nothing wrong in aspiring to the top and added that her father had once told her any politician worth their salt harboured this ambition. She also reassured Sonia that he never held it against her after she changed the subject, describing him as pragmatic. The memoir also details an unspoken division of responsibility between Sonia and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh (2004 to 2014). Sonia rejected a 'back-seat driver' charge, calling related allegations from a former aide's book malicious and false, while Upinder Singh defended her father's relationship with Gandhi as built on mutual trust.
items.title: Pranab Mukherjee's daughter rebuts Sonia Gandhi over his PM ambition

items.summary: In Meghalaya, local communities are turning fragile limestone caves into carefully managed tourist sites to protect them while creating village jobs. Mawmluh Cave near Cherrapunji holds a stalagmite chosen as the marker for the Meghalayan Age, formally recognised in 2018, tied to a climate event about 4,200 years ago. Scientists warn that erratic rainfall and decades of unregulated mining threaten these formations; an illegal mine explosion earlier this year killed 27 miners. Guides like Milton Marak keep caves natural, admitting only 25 visitors daily. Geologist Jaishree Sanwal Bhatt cautions ecotourism cannot shoulder conservation alone without stronger regulation and scientific monitoring.
items.title: Meghalaya Communities Guard Ancient Caves Through Tourism

items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization said in a Monday report that 2026 is on track to be one of the four warmest years on record, with global average temperature between January and September about 1.47 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. The agency attributed early-year cooling to La Niña conditions reversed by El Niño development by June, which it forecast would continue into early 2027. Secretary General Celeste Saulo said the ongoing El Niño is expected to be one of the strongest on record and will fuel high temperatures through 2027.
items.title: UN Weather Agency Forecasts Record-Warm 2026

items.summary: Police arrested three men on Monday in Greater Noida for running an online cannabis supply network that used Telegram and e-commerce-style parcel deliveries. The seizure included 55 kg and 124 grams of cannabis, estimated by police to be worth ₹55 lakh, plus a sedan car and three mobile phones. According to the deputy commissioner of police Praveen Ranjan Singh, they procured cannabis from Odisha and other areas, repackaged it in bags resembling e-commerce brands, and delivered orders on demand. A case was registered under sections 8 and 20 of the NDPS Act at Bisrakh police station; investigation into sources and buyers continues.
items.title: Three Arrested Over Telegram Drug Network in Greater Noida

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi recounts in her autobiography Belonging: A Journey of Love, released Tuesday, the loss of her first child, a premature baby boy who died shortly after birth on January 18, 1969. She describes learning she was expecting in September 1969 and the preparations that followed, including dietary instructions from her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi. The couple fell in love with their son before he died at 6:30 in the morning. Grief compounded by a right-wing newspaper report calling him a bastard child led Rajiv and Sanjay Gandhi to bury him beneath a bougainvillea bush on the family's Mehrauli farm rather than release his remains into a river, which Hindu tradition permitted for newborns.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Recalls Losing Her First Child and His Burial

items.summary: The Centre is expanding high-value marine fishing in Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under its Blue Economy strategy, prioritising tuna, seaweed cultivation and ornamental fish. Under PMMSY it allocated ₹218 crore to the Andamans and ₹175 crore to Lakshadweep for a combined ₹393 crore. Officials emphasise scientific exploitation over indiscriminate fishing, value-chain benefits for local communities and conservation of coral reefs amid production goals.
items.title: India backs island tuna and seaweed fisheries

items.summary: Sharmistha Mukherjee, daughter of former President Pranab Mukherjee, challenged her sister-in-law Sonia Gandhi after the latter said she was shocked by a 2010 hint that Pranab wanted to become Prime Minister. Sharmistha defended his record and dismissed dynastic entitlements as unfair, arguing merit earned his positions between 2004 and 2012. She questioned why ambition outside the Gandhi-Nehru family should be surprising.
items.title: Pranab Mukherjee's Daughter Rebuts Sonia Gandhi Over His PM Ambition

items.summary: This excerpt from Objects and Memories from Goa describes the khun, a traditional conical bamboo fish trap once found in nearly every rural Goan home. Made from woven bamboo strips with a crown called a mugda and an inside-opening valve that lets fish in but not out, it was considered essential survival equipment for fishing in swift rivers and springs. The text also mentions related traps—the doba and the nada—as well as other local tools like the tope pot used by children. While these methods once defined community life around fishing, the author observes they have largely been replaced today by plastic carrier bags and money.
items.title: Traditional Goan Fish Traps Fade as Modern Life Takes Over
